name: pdescprec
description: REVIEW_Aug4 A4-H05 descriptor-fault-precedence regression plus protected far-pointer-load atomicity. The original 16 cases are eight combined-invalid discriminators and eight presence-only controls across MOV Sreg, far JMP, IDT gates, interrupt target CS (GDT and LDT), and RETF. Case 17 executes LDS ESI,m16:32 with a P=0 selector and proves #NP(0x30) leaves ESI unchanged; this prevents a decoder-only LDS repair from exposing its offset half before descriptor validation. Every delivery records {handler-CS<<16|vector} and its error code, and the image verifies all 34 slot dwords. The ring-3 body explicitly reloads valid DS=0x23 after each fault return; its handler's DPL0 DS is correctly nulled by an outer IRET. This avoids depending on QEMU's permissive null-data-access behavior without weakening descriptor-fault grading.
transitions: real->protected via a 17-entry GDT (limit 0x87): flat code0/data0, ring-3 code3/data3, eleven P=0 test descriptors (access 0x12 = S|data, 0x72 = S|DPL3|data, 0x1A = S|code, 0x02 = LDT), one 32-bit TSS (0x78), one present LDT descriptor (0x80 -> LDT @0x3000); CR0.PE 0->1

IDT @ 0x1000: vectors 11/12/13 -> np/ss/gp handlers, 8/14 -> fail exits, 32 = P=0 LDT descriptor (illegal gate type), 33 = P=0 legal int32 gate, 34/35 = present int32 gates targeting GDT selectors 0x68 (P=0 data) / 0x70 (P=0 code), 36/37 = present int32 gates targeting LDT selectors 0x000C (P=0 data) / 0x0014 (P=0 code)
fam 1a: DS <- 0x28 (P=0 LDT desc, S=0) -> #GP(0x28); control DS <- 0x30 (P=0 valid data) -> #NP(0x30)
fam 1c: SS <- 0x48 (P=0 code desc, not writable data) -> #GP(0x48); control SS <- 0x50 (P=0 writable data, DPL=CPL=RPL=0) -> #SS(0x50)
fam 2: direct ljmp -> 0x58 (P=0 DATA) -> #GP(0x58); control ljmp -> 0x60 (P=0 code) -> #NP(0x60)
fam 3: int $32 with IDT[32] a P=0 LDT descriptor -> #GP(0x102 = 32*8+2); control int $33 with a P=0 legal int32 gate -> #NP(0x10A = 33*8+2)
fam 4: int $34 through a present gate naming P=0 DATA target CS 0x68 -> #GP(0x68); control int $35 naming P=0 code target CS 0x70 -> #NP(0x70)

fam 4b: LLDT 0x80 (LDT @0x3000: null / P=0 data / P=0 code / null); int $36 through a present gate naming LDT target CS 0x000C (TI=1, P=0 DATA) -> #GP(0x000C, TI preserved); control int $37 naming LDT target CS 0x0014 (TI=1, P=0 code) -> #NP(0x0014, TI preserved); in-guest bit asserts on both pushed codes (TI=1, IDT=0, EXT=0; fail edi = 0x94/0x95/0x96)
fam 5: same-privilege RETF popping CS=0x58 (P=0 DATA) -> #GP(0x58); control popping CS=0x60 (P=0 code) -> #NP(0x60); ESP preserved across the rejected RETFs (H-02, both oracles)
fam 7: LDS ESI,m16:32 at 0x2200 with offset 0xDEADBEEF and P=0 selector 0x30 -> #NP(0x30); ESI remains its pre-instruction sentinel 0xA55A1234 (atomic two-destination rejection)
IOPL=3 + outer RETF to ring 3 (TSS SS0:ESP0 for the cross-privilege deliveries)
fam 1b: DS <- 0x38 (P=0 data DPL=0) at CPL3 -> #GP(0x38); control DS <- 0x40 (P=0 data DPL=3) at CPL3 -> #NP(0x40)
exit: verify all 34 slot dwords against exptab (fail edi = 0x80|cases-remaining), check the delivery counters (fail edi = 0x90/0x91/0x92/0x93), fold, isa-debug-exit at CPL==IOPL==3 (status 133)

fam4c.intent: a HARDWARE interrupt delivered through an IDT gate whose target CS is bad (P=0 data) must raise #GP(sel & 0xfffc | EXT=1) per SDM Vol.3A 6.13 (EXT=1: the exception occurs during delivery of an event external to the program)
fam4c.blocker: no deterministic hardware-interrupt injection exists in the --system testbench: tb_main.cpp drives top->intr ONLY inside #ifdef VEN_DOS_MODELS + args.dos (the PIT/PIC IRQ0 pump, tb_main.cpp:1492-1543); in --system mode top->intr is tied to 0 for the whole run (tb_main.cpp:1263). The DOS models additionally need sw/ps_periph/*.c, which is absent from this checkout. And the golden side cannot observe a hardware IRQ at all: the qemu-system gdbstub single-step path masks external interrupts (the same SSTEP_NOIRQ infeasibility psmm documents for SMI). Fabricating a cycle-timed injection would be a flaky test, so fam 4c is documented here instead -- see oracle_gaps.

witnesses.differential grading: Full per-instruction register compare against pinned QEMU; every witness flows through a register twice (handler store + exit-loop verify/fold), so any vector/error-code divergence or premature LDS GPR commit breaks the diff at its first visible record. The repaired fixture passed fresh enforcing-profile qualification on 2026-10-01: all 2572 records match pinned QEMU. The historical pre-repair permissive-profile trace had 2568 records.

oracle_gaps: 2026-10-01 fixture repair: the enforcing RTL and pinned QEMU agreed through n=2318, PC 0xF0668 (IRETL), including returned CS=0x1B/SS=0x23/ESP=0x5000 and DS=0. The next instruction at 0xF0501 was a default-DS store to CURSLOT, not a failed IRET. The RTL correctly delivered #GP(0) for that null-DS use while QEMU allowed it. Two register-only DS=0x23 reloads now follow the two ring-3 fault returns, before the next DS-relative access. All 17 descriptor cases, handlers, frame offsets, expected vectors/error codes, and final witnesses are unchanged. Fresh frozen enforcing-TB/pinned-QEMU qualification passed all 2572 records, and the separately closed normal-I/O RTL run delivered exactly 8 #GP, 8 #NP, and 1 #SS, with no other faults. The historical 2,568-record permissive-profile result below is retained only as history.

(RETIRED 2026-08-04) the fam-4 target-CS error-code bit-1 form gap is closed: the RTL now blames the gate's target CS selector with TI from the selector / IDT=0 / EXT=0 for a software INT (selector_error_ext in ventium_sys_pkg.sv, used by core_int_deliver.svh) -- exactly QEMU's `selector & 0xfffc` form. The NOSTORE workaround is removed and fam 4 is fully differential like every other family.

(OPEN 2026-08-05, fam 4c) EXT=1 for an EXTERNALLY-delivered source: per SDM Vol.3A 6.13, a #GP/#NP raised while delivering a hardware interrupt or NMI through a gate with a bad target CS must push the target selector's error code with EXT=1 (the RTL's selector_error_ext(int_gate_sel, !int_sw) implements this). QEMU 8.2.2 cannot be the oracle: do_interrupt_protected in ventium-refs/07-p5-emulation-harness/build/qemu/target/i386/tcg/seg_helper.c pushes `selector & 0xfffc` (lines 689/699) -- EXT=0 ALWAYS, regardless of the event source (is_hw only feeds back into HF/RF handling, never the error code). A witness-graded run is ALSO infeasible in this harness: the --system testbench never drives the core's intr input (top->intr is tied to 0 outside the VEN_DOS_MODELS --dos PIT/PIC pump, tb_main.cpp:1263 vs 1492-1543, and the DOS models' sw/ps_periph sources are absent from this checkout), and the qemu-system gdbstub single-step path masks external interrupts entirely (the psmm SSTEP_NOIRQ precedent), so no deterministic injection + observation point exists on either side. Documented, not tested -- no flaky test fabricated.

scoped_down.family 6 (task switch): SUPERSEDED 2026-08-05 -- the scoping rationale below is no longer the RTL's behavior. The S_LJMP system-descriptor dispatch is now a typed classifier in the pinned oracle's precedence (type/DPL before presence; the default-case #GP for outright-rejected classes; the loud halt survives only for task gate / 286 TSS / NT-return-to-non-busy, after the architecturally required faults). The combined-invalid shapes this note described as deliberately presence-first are now differentially reachable and are covered by pxfer's combined-invalid matrix (P=0+wrong-type and P=0+DPL for available/busy TSS, LDT, task gate, and call gate, each with a presence-only control). History: SKIPPED -- not differentially reachable in this core, for two independent reasons. (a) QEMU checks a direct far transfer's TSS-descriptor TYPE and DPL in helper_ljmp_protected (the case-1/9/5 switch and its default -> #GP) BEFORE switch_tss_ra's presence check, so a P=0 wrong-type or P=0 DPL-failing TSS-slot descriptor is #GP in QEMU. The RTL deliberately evaluates PRESENCE FIRST for system descriptors on a far transfer (core_seg_ljmp.svh: 'an ABSENT system descriptor is #NP(selector), not the unsupported-form halt -- presence precedes unimplemented', R2-C01) and loud-HALTs every non-TSS system descriptor form (H-19: task gate 0xD5, LDT 0xD2, 16-bit TSS -- documented in docs/unsupported-isa.md). The A4-H05 fix intentionally did not touch that order. (b) Within the implemented TSS forms (type 9/0xB), the combined-invalid shapes either hit (a)'s deliberate presence-first rule or are order-ambiguous in QEMU itself (switch_tss_ra checks P before the busy form). A #NP-only control (P=0 valid available TSS) would prove nothing about precedence, so the whole family is scoped out rather than pinned dishonestly.

negative_control.method_2026_08_05: MEASURED for the target-CS error-code form: a scratch copy of the RTL tree (tmp/pdescneg/rtl, since removed) had core_int_deliver.svh's two `selector_error_ext(int_gate_sel, !int_sw)` calls restored to the pre-fix `{16'd0, int_gate_sel[15:3], 3'b010}` form (drops TI, forces IDT=1), built into a scratch objdir with `make -C verif/tb rtl OBJDIR=obj_dir_pdescneg RTL_DIR=<scratch>/rtl` (the canonical verif/tb/obj_dir untouched), and run on this image. Result: +ven_faultlog shows `vec=13 err=0000000a` for the fam-4b discriminator (int $36, selector 0x000C -> old form 0x000A: TI dropped, IDT set) and `vec=13 err=0000006a` / `vec=11 err=00000072` for fam 4; compare.py vs the golden is DIVERGENT from n=2136 (eax 0x6A vs 0x68) and the guest then stops at the fam-4b TI bit assert -- the negative trace's final record is edi=eax=0x00000094 (bit_ti_fail), 2189 records vs the golden's 2531. The canonical RTL was byte-identical afterwards (md5 72afe731d4f6621f5ebe2c0daa409836).
negative_control.pre_fix_logic: seg_load_fault evaluated `if (!desc_present(a)) fault = 1'b1; // #NP / #SS` FIRST, before the S/type/privilege chain; seg_fault_vec returned #NP(11)/#SS(12) for ANY non-null not-present descriptor (`if (!nullsel && !desc_present(a)) vec = is_ss ? 12 : 11; else 13`). The IDT gate arm checked the gate's Present bit before its type, and the target-CS arm was a collapsed cs_bad with 'NP iff P=0' and the `{sel[15:3],3'b010}` error form. The A4-H05 fix reordered all four sites: S/type/privilege -> #GP, presence LAST -> #NP/#SS, and the selector_error_ext error form.
negative_control.expected_pre_fix: all eight combined-invalid cases deliver #NP where the oracle says #GP (fam1a #NP(0x28), fam1b #NP(0x38), fam1c #SS(0x48) -- the is_ss form, fam2 #NP(0x58), fam3 #NP(0x102), fam4 #NP(sel), fam4b #NP(sel), fam5 #NP(0x58)): np_handler/ss_handler run instead of gp_handler, the {cs<<16|vec} slot words lose 0x0D and gain 0x0B/0x0C, the exptab verify fails at the first case (edi=0x90), and the differential diverges at np_handler's first record. The eight single-invalid controls are invisible to the precedence defect (presence is their sole failure) -- they pass pre- and post-fix, making the test non-vacuous by construction. The error-FORM half of the pre-fix state is the measured control above.
